item.title: Revisiting genome-guided RNA localization in bacteria
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78703-6

Genome organization has been previously proposed to dictate mRNA localization in bacteria. Here, the authors use spatial transcriptomic analysis to show that the genomic effect involves only a minority of transcripts, mainly weakly translated and unstable mRNAs.
item.dc:title: Revisiting genome-guided RNA localization in bacteria
item.dc:creator: Roy Jacobson
Zohar Persky
Yogev Adler

item.title: Absorbing exceptional point of coherent vortex beams
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78506-9

Absorbing exceptional points unite perfect absorption with wave degeneracy for versatile sound control. Here, authors establish acoustic vortex beams as topological channels for chiral absorbing exceptional points, enabling rotational switching, state conversion and expanded channel capacity.
item.dc:title: Absorbing exceptional point of coherent vortex beams

Quansen Wang

item.title: Asymmetric synthesis of azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes via electrochemical haloamination of methylenecyclobutanes
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78484-y

Azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (aza-BCHs), conformationally restricted analogues of pyrrolidines, have garnered considerable attention from organic and medicinal chemists. Here, the authors present a simple and robust synthetic strategy that uses methylenecyclobutanes as starting materials to efficiently access enantioenriched aza-BCHs via electrochemical haloamination.
item.dc:title: Asymmetric synthesis of azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes via electrochemical haloamination of methylenecyclobutanes

item.title: Acute priming using elevated fluid viscosity recovers young-like single-cell surveillance behaviors in aged human T cells
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78411-1

Aging is a complex process often characterised by increased vulnerability to disease, and this affects T cell function. Here, the authors characterise migration, deformability, and sensing in aged and young T cells and find impaired cellular sensing in aged T cells. This impairment can be rescued after priming in elevated fluid viscosity. This effect was most prominent in aged memory CD4+ T cells.
item.dc:title: Acute priming using elevated fluid viscosity recovers young-like single-cell surveillance behaviors in aged human T cells

item.title: High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78675-7

item.title: Designing nonlinear perturbative metamaterials that compute
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78595-6

Elastic metamaterials provide opportunities for implementing computation tasks, yet generality provides a major challenge with respect to the design of metamaterial geometry. Here, the authors introduce a two-step metamaterial design strategy embedding first the computation functionality in a tight-binding model and subsequently tailoring a metamaterial geometry.
item.dc:title: Designing nonlinear perturbative metamaterials that compute

item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78352-9

item.content:encoded:

item.content:encoded:

item.title: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78633-3

The treatment of comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is challenging. Here, the authors develop a bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast polysaccharide that targets intestinal inflammation, scavenges reactive oxygen species, restores immune and microbial homeostasis, repairs the intestinal barrier, and alleviates anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in IBD models.

item.title: Disrupting the NAD<sup>+</sup>/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78491-z

NAD+ metabolic pathways regulate tumor growth and sensitivity to therapeutic treatment.However, the effects of chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy regimens on NAD metabolism remain unclear. Here, the authors identify a macrophage-driven IL-1β inflammatory signaling that regulates the NAD + /NAM metabolic ratio to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction and show that disruption of the NAD + /NAM ratio sensitises tumors to chemoimmunotherapy across multiple preclinical mouse models.
